crossover

A Game Boy + SNES emulator with a shared hub world. Portable C99, SDL2.

crossover.exe174 KB · x86-64 · Windows SDL2.dll1.7 MB · required, same folder as the exe README.txtcontrols, limits, build instructions Source tarball75 KB · full C99 tree

Run it

crossover.exe --snes  game.smc    # SNES ROM (LoROM or HiROM)
crossover.exe --gb    game.gb     # Game Boy ROM

Download crossover.exe and SDL2.dll into the same folder and double-click the exe. A console window opens for diagnostics.

Controller support

Any SDL2 game controller works and is hot-plugged. On a DualSense Edge (Sony $054C:$0DF2, USB and Bluetooth) the pad is named on connect and mapped like this:

SNESDualSense Edge
A (right)Circle
B (bottom)Cross
X (top)Triangle
Y (left)Square
L / RL1 / R1, or L2 / R2 past half-press
Select / StartShare or mic button / Options or PS button
D-padD-pad, or either stick past the deadzone

The Edge needs SDL2 ≥ 2.26.5; this build links 2.32.10.

Status. All 304 headless checks pass and Super Mario World boots to gameplay rendering (APU handshake, Mode 1 layers, sprites). The build has not yet been play-tested interactively; the SNES core has no ExHiROM and no enhancement chips. See README.txt for the full list.

Build it yourself

x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc -std=c99 -O2 -DUSE_SDL2 \
  -I SDL2-2.32.10/x86_64-w64-mingw32/include -I core -I platform \
  core/*.c platform/frontend.c platform/main_win.c -o crossover.exe \
  -L SDL2-2.32.10/x86_64-w64-mingw32/lib \
  -lmingw32 -lSDL2main -lSDL2 -lgdi32 -luser32 -limm32 -lole32 \
  -lwinmm -lsetupapi -lhid -lcfgmgr32 -lversion -lshell32 -mwindows

Headless core, no SDL2 needed: make test
